chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me of it, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amir, from 'Ali ibn Mahziyar; and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from 'Ali ibn Mahziyar; and 'Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from 'Ali ibn Mahziyar, who said:

I read in a letter that 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad wrote to Abū al-Hasan عليه السلام: “May I be your ransom, Zurarah has narrated from Abū Ja'far and Abū 'Abd Allah عليهما السلام regarding wine that affects the garment and the foot, that they both said: There is no problem in praying in it; only its drinking has been forbidden.”

And someone other than Zurarah narrated from Abū 'Abd Allah عليه السلام that he said: “If wine or nabidh — meaning the intoxicating kind — reaches your garment, then wash it if you know its place; and if you do not know its place, then wash all of it. If you prayed in it, then repeat your salat (prayer). So inform me which of them I should follow.”

So he wrote back in his own hand عليه السلام, and I read it: “Take the statement of Abū 'Abd Allah عليه السلام.” Thus he instructed him to adopt the statement of Abū 'Abd Allah عليه السلام which entails prohibition, and to leave his statement along with the statement of Abū Ja'far عليه السلام which entails permissibility. This indicates that that earlier report was issued by way of taqiyyah, because if it had not been so, then taking both of their statements together would have been more appropriate. Moreover, in none of the later reports that we have cited is there anything stating that there is no problem with praying in garments affected by wine; rather, he was only asked about a garment touched by wine, and he said: “There is no problem with it.” It is possible that this was a negation of prohibition concerning wearing it and benefiting from it, even if salat (prayer) in it is not permissible.

key_terms.التَّحْرِيمَ: prohibition; the legal implication of the preferred report
key_terms.التَّقِيَّةِ: taqiyyah; precautionary dissimulation indicated as the context of the other narration
key_terms.النَّبِيذُ: nabidh; here specified as the intoxicating type
key_terms.الْإِبَاحَةَ: permissibility; the implication of the other report
key_terms.الْخَمْرِ: wine; the intoxicating substance discussed in relation to garments and salat (prayer)
key_terms.فَأَعِدْ صَلَاتَكَ: repeat your salat (prayer); the ruling if one prayed in the affected garment
key_terms.فَاغْسِلْهُ: wash it; the instruction for purifying the garment

ai.seo_question: What should be followed when hadith reports differ about praying in clothes touched by wine?
ai.summary: This report addresses the ruling on garments affected by wine or intoxicating nabidh and how to act when hadith reports appear to conflict. The instruction given is to follow the report of Abū 'Abd Allah عليه السلام requiring washing the garment and repeating the salat (prayer) if one prayed in it, while the contrary report is treated as having been issued under taqiyyah.
